guard: a space catalog is applied to the registry under the provider's lock, with the cache saying the snapshot is not applied until the consumer's last write has happened, so a command that dies or pauses while applying leaves a cache the next command repairs instead of a partial registry it accepts as fresh
why: The provider committed a fetched snapshot to its cache and released the catalog lock before the CLI wrote the registry one entry at a time. Measured at b260c3776 with the built components in real child processes: a sync killed after the first registry rename left the registry with one of three discovered spaces while the cache reported the whole snapshot as current; every later command inside the freshness window used that registry with zero requests, and after the window a conditional 304 confirmed it. Only an explicit sync repaired it. A second process could also list the half-written set while the first was still writing.

The suite drives the shipped prepareIdpSpaceCatalogs with the consumer's apply and reads the cache file between calls. It does not kill a process: the cells plant the cache state a death leaves behind (applied false), because that state is the contract the recovery rests on, and one cell observes the commit order from inside apply, which is the only vantage a paused process has.

Three mutations, each on the boundary and not on a message: skipping the pre-write commit makes the observed-order cell red because the cache inside apply still names the previous ETag; dropping the re-application makes the zero-request repair cell red because the provider answers fresh with nothing handed to the consumer; never recording applied makes the settled cell red because the consumer is handed an updated result on every warm call and the count check catches the second application.

mutations.name: the candidate is not committed to the cache before the consumer's first registry write
mutations.expectRed: a fetched candidate is committed as not applied before the consumer's first write and as applied after its last
mutations.cell: a fetched candidate is committed as not applied before the consumer's first write and as applied after its last

mutations.name: a cached snapshot whose application never finished is never applied again
mutations.expectRed: a cached snapshot whose application never finished is applied again inside the freshness window with zero requests
mutations.cell: a cached snapshot whose application never finished is applied again inside the freshness window with zero requests

mutations.name: a fetched candidate is never recorded as applied after the consumer returns
mutations.expectRed: an applied snapshot inside the window is reported fresh and handed to the consumer no more
mutations.cell: an applied snapshot inside the window is reported fresh and handed to the consumer no more
